questions.question: What solution should be used to test for the presence of starch in food?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iodine solution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Iodine solution** is commonly used to test for the presence of starch in food items.
 
• When iodine solution is applied to a substance containing starch, it reacts to form a **blue-black color**, indicating the presence of starch.
 
• The reaction occurs because iodine molecules interact with the helical structure of amylose, a component of starch.
 
• This test is highly specific to starch and does not produce similar reactions with other carbohydrates like glucose or sucrose.
 
• Iodine solution is prepared by dissolving iodine in potassium iodide and water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Starch:**

 
 
• Starch is a polysaccharide composed of glucose units linked together, commonly found in plants.
 
• It is a major source of energy in the human diet, present in foods like potatoes, rice, and wheat.
 
 
 
• **Amylose and Amylopectin:**
 
 
• Starch consists of two components: **amylose** (linear chains) and **amylopectin** (branched chains).
 
• The iodine solution primarily reacts with amylose to produce the blue-black coloration.
 
 
 
• **Iodine Solution Preparation:**
 
 
• Iodine solution is created by dissolving iodine crystals in a potassium iodide solution, which increases iodine's solubility in water.
 
• It is often diluted before use in laboratory experiments.
 
 
 
• **Other Applications of Iodine Solution:**
 
 
• Besides starch testing, iodine solution is used as a disinfectant and antiseptic in medical applications.
 
• It is also employed in titration experiments to determine the concentration of substances in chemistry.

questions.question: Liver gland secretes ________ that is stored in a sac called the gall bladder.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __liver__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bile is secreted by the liver.

 
 
• Bile is a fluid that is made and released by the liver and stored in the gallbladder.
 
• Bile helps with digestion.
 
• It breaks down fats into fatty acids, which can be taken into the body by the digestive tract.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mucous is a viscous secretion** that is produced by mucous membranes, and it helps in lubricating and protecting the tissues. It is not secreted by the liver gland.
 
• **Hydrochloric acid** is a strong acid that is secreted by the stomach lining, and it helps in the breakdown of food particles. It is not secreted by the liver gland.
 
• **Estrogen is a hormone** that is produced by the ovaries in females, and it plays a vital role in the development of secondary sexual characteristics. It is not secreted by the liver gland.

questions.question: Snails is an example of which of the phylum of animal kingdom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mollusca**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mollusca:-**

 
 
• **Molluscs are characterized by their soft bodies, which are often protected by a hard shell. **
 
• They also have a unique digestive system that includes a muscular foot, a radula (a tongue-like organ with rows of teeth), and a gizzard. 
 
• Molluscs are divided into several classes, including the Gastropoda (snails and slugs), Bivalvia (clams and oysters), Cephalopoda (squids, octopuses, and nautiluses), and Polyplacophora (chitons).
 
• **Snails are an example of the phylum Mollusca.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Arthropoda:-**

 
 
• **It is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom, comprising about 80% of all known animal species. **
 
• Arthropods live in all habitats on Earth, from the sea to the air, and from the poles to the tropics.
 
 
 
• **Protochordates:-**
 
 
• **These are an informal category of animals that are closely related to vertebrates. **
 
• They are invertebrates, but they share many of the same characteristics as vertebrates, such as a notochord (a flexible rod that runs along the back of the animal), a dorsal nerve cord, and pharyngeal gill slits.
 
 
 
• **Annelida:-**
 
 
• **It is a phylum of segmented worms, with over 22,000 extant species including ragworms, earthworms, and leeches. **
 
• The species exist in and have adapted to various ecologies – some in marine environments as distinct as tidal zones and hydrothermal vents, others in fresh water, and yet others in moist terrestrial environments.

questions.question: Mosquito belongs to ________ phylum of the animal kingdom.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arthropoda.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mosquito **belongs to the **phylum Arthropoda** in the animal kingdom.
 
• The Arthropoda phylum includes **insects, spiders, crustaceans**, and other arthropods. 
 
• **Arthropods are characterized by their jointed appendages and exoskeletons.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mosquitoes** are further classified as members of the family Culicidae within the order Diptera, which also includes flies.
 
• **Ctenophora is a phylum of marine animals commonly known as comb jellies.**
 
• **Chordata is a phylum that includes animals with spinal cords such as mammals and fish.**
 
• **Mollusca **is a phylum of animals that includes **snails, clams, and octopuses.**

questions.question: What is the primary gas responsible for the leavening effect in bread when yeast ferments sugars?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is the primary gas responsible for the leavening effect in bread when yeast ferments sugars.
 
• Yeast, a microorganism, consumes the sugars present in the dough and produces carbon dioxide and alcohol as by-products.
 
• The carbon dioxide gas gets trapped within the dough, causing it to expand and rise, resulting in the soft and airy texture of bread.
 
• Besides carbon dioxide, the fermentation process also produces ethanol, but this evaporates during baking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yeast Fermentation:**

 
 
• Yeast fermentation is a metabolic process that converts sugar into acids, gases, or alcohol.
 
• Saccharomyces cerevisiae is the most commonly used yeast in bread making.
 
 
 
• **Leavening Agents:**
 
 
• Leavening agents are substances used in dough and batter to produce a foaming action, which lightens and softens the finished product.
 
• Besides yeast, other leavening agents include baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) and baking powder.
 
 
 
• **Proofing:**
 
 
• Proofing is the process of allowing dough to rise before baking.
 
• During proofing, yeast ferments the dough, producing carbon dioxide and causing the dough to expand.
 
 
 
• **Gluten:**
 
 
• Gluten is a protein found in wheat, barley, and rye that gives dough its elasticity.
 
• It helps trap carbon dioxide produced by yeast, aiding in the rising process.

questions.question: Which among the following is an example of Phylum Mammalia of Animal Kingdom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rat.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mammalia:-

 
 
• The word "Mammalia" comes from the Latin word "mamma," which means "breast" or "udder."
 
• This is because mammals produce milk to feed their young.
 
• Some other examples of animals belonging to the Phylum Mammalia are humans, dogs, cats, whales, and elephants. 
 
• Rat belongs to the Phylum Mammalia of the Animal Kingdom.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Crocodiles** are large reptiles that are found in freshwater habitats.
 
• 
 
 
• They have a** long and powerful tail, sharp teeth,** and a tough skin.
 
 
 
• **Hens** are domesticated birds that are commonly kept for their eggs and meat.
 
 
• They have a **beak, feathers, and wings, **and are known for their clucking sound.
 
 
 
• **Pigeons** are also domesticated birds that are often used for racing, as messenger birds, or as pets.
 
 
• They have a **plump body, short neck, and small head.**

questions.question: Which of the following is the richest source of Vitamin C?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lemon.​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lemons contain about 31 grams of Vitamin C.
 
• It is also known as ascorbic acid and is found in citrus fruits (like orange, and lemon), kiwifruit, guava, broccoli, strawberries, etc. 
 
• It is an essential nutrient and is not synthesized by the human body. It is a water-soluble vitamin.
 
• Functions - Repair of tissues, acts as a co-factor in many enzymatic reactions, important for the Immune system, acts as an antioxidant.
 
• C6H8O6 is the chemical formula of Vitamin C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• It is on the List of Essential Medicines of the World Health Organization.
 
• Deficiency Disease - The deficiency of Vitamin C causes scurvy. 
 
• Discovery - It was discovered in 1912 and first isolated in 1928.

questions.question: Which among the following is Phanerogams, flowering and seed - bearing plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gymnosperms.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phanerogams:-**

 
 
• **​**These are plants that produce **flowers and seeds** and are also known as **angiosperms.**
 
 
 
• **Gymnosperms:-**
 
 
• Gymnosperms are a group of seed-producing plants that includes conifers, cycads, Ginkgo, and gnetophytes.
 
• Gymnosperms are known as "naked seed" plants because their seeds are not enclosed in a fruit. Instead, the seeds are exposed on the surface of the plant, often in cones.
 
• Some examples of gymnosperms:
 
 
• Conifers: Pines, firs, spruces, cedars, etc.
 
• Cycads: Sago palms, etc.
 
• Ginkgo: Ginkgo biloba
 
• Gnetophytes: Welwitschia, Ephedra, Gnetum
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pteridophyta :-

 
 
• Pteridophyta, also known as ferns, are a group of vascular plants that reproduce by spores.
 
• They are the first group of plants to evolve vascular tissue, which allows them to transport water and nutrients throughout their bodies.
 
• Pteridophytes are also the first group of plants to have true leaves.
 
 
 
• **Bryophyta**:-
 
 
• It is also known as mosses, liverworts, and hornworts, are a group of non-vascular plants that reproduce by spores.
 
• They are the most primitive group of land plants, and they are found in a wide variety of habitats, including forests, wetlands, and even deserts.
 
 
 
• **Thallophyta**:-
 
 
• It is a polyphyletic group of non-mobile organisms that are traditionally described as "thalloid plants", "relatively simple plants" or "lower plants".
 
• They form a division of kingdom Plantae that include lichens and algae and occasionally bryophytes, bacteria and slime moulds.

questions.question: Cytology is the study of ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cells.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cytology is the branch of biology that deals with the study of cells and their structure, functions, and interactions with other cells.
 
• It involves the examination of cells under the microscope to understand their morphology, physiology, and biochemistry.
 
• Cytology is important in fields such as genetics, pathology, and cancer research.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chloroplasts** are organelles found in** plant cells** that are responsible for **photosynthesis.**
 
• **Tissues **are groups of cells that perform a** specific function** in an organism.
 
• **Genes **are the **basic units of heredity** that carry information for the development and **function of cells and organisms. **

questions.question: Which of the following acids is found in spinach?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oxalic acid.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oxalic acid** is found in **spinach**.
 
• Oxalic acid is a crystalline substance that dissolves in water to create a colorless solution.
 
• Food items such as **spinach and cabbage, broccoli, parsley, and tomatoes contain it**.
 
• Oxalic acid is extensively used as an acid rinse in laundries because it is good for removing rust and ink stains.
 
• It is the most basic dicarboxylic acid. It is a white crystalline substance that converts most insoluble iron compounds into soluble complex ions in water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tartaric acid** is a white, crystalline organic acid found naturally in many fruits, including grapes, bananas, tamarinds, and citrus.
 
• **Lactic acid** is generated primarily by muscle cells and red blood cells. It is found primarily in dairy products.
 
• **Citrus fruits**, particularly lemons and limes, contain naturally occurring **citric acid**.
 
 
• **Citric acid** in its synthetic form is extensively used as an additive in food, cleaning products, and nutritional supplements.
 
 
 
• **The formic acid** formula is written as HCOOH which contains two hydrogen atoms, and two oxygen atoms attached to only one central carbon atom.
 
 
• Formic acid is obtained from** red ants.**
